haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized before any Redis call, so no rate-limit counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: Counters use the customer ID, not the API key, so all keys share one budget: 100 requests per minute for Standard.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After seconds and a small JSON error body. The backend never sees the request.
haiku-low.q4: No. The script increments only when it allows a request, so 429 responses cost no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The increment happens before forwarding, so a backend 500 still counts against the budget.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway fails open: it forwards the request, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and omits X-RateLimit-* headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. The Enterprise limit is open, undecided, and Enterprise requests are not counted.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, under key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Counts expire after 120 seconds, outliving the 60-second window.
haiku-low.q9: Fixed one-minute windows: each new window starts at count zero when windowStart changes, based on Redis time.
haiku-low.q10: Redis runs check_and_incr atomically, one script at a time, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: retryAfter = max(1, windowStart + 60 - redisTime), in whole seconds, computed inside the Redis script.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for retries. The request is forwarded without X-RateLimit-* headers, and a metric is emitted.

sonnet.q1: Gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. No Redis call, so no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Counter key uses customer ID, not API key, so all three keys share one budget: the customer's single limit (100/min if Standard; Enterprise limit undecided).
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds) and a small JSON error body; no X-RateLimit-* headers. The backend never sees it; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. The script increments only when it allows a request, so 429s cost no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The increment happens before forwarding, so it counts even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: Fails open: the gateway emits metric ratelimit_store_unavailable and forwards the request to the backend, returning the backend response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: not decided (open); until then Enterprise requests are forwarded uncounted with no Redis call.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Redis, under key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Keys are set to expire after 120 s when the count first becomes 1, which removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: Fixed one-minute windows: when the next window starts (windowStart = floor(redisTime/60)*60, using Redis time) a new counter key begins at 0. Old key expires after 120 s.
sonnet.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs atomically inside Redis (scripts run one at a time), reading the count and incrementing only if count < limit, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: retryAfter = max(1, windowStart + 60 - redisTime), in whole seconds, computed in the script from Redis time.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers, just the backend response.
